key_facts: Council Bill 1421 seeks to rezone a parcel at 14 2038 street from its current R.M. 30 with waivers zoning to CMC's eight zoning.
The property is currently vacant with some building footings remaining and is located directly across the street from the 38th and Blake RTD Station.
The request is to allow the relocation of the tiny home village currently operating on a property on Walnut, just over the alley from the subject site.
The tiny home village operates under a six-month temporary unlisted use permit, which does not apply to former Chapter 59 zoning.
The rezoning request is consistent with the recommendations of the 38th and Blake Station area height amendments adopted in 2016.
The tiny home village has provided nearly 2700 nights of safe, dignified housing to people who would otherwise be on the streets in 180 days of operation.
The village has operated at a cost of $5.80 per person per night.
The proposed rezoning is supported by the Urban Land Conservancy, the Colorado Village Collaborative, and the Black Star Action Movement for Self-defense.
The rezoning request is part of the larger 38th and Blake Project base rezoning, which is set to be considered next month.
The rezoning request has had extensive public outreach and multiple meetings and workshops.
The rezoning request meets the five criteria from the Denver zoning code for adopting a zone change.
The rezoning request is expected to pass with a unanimous vote.
The tiny home village is scheduled to move from its current location by January 12th.
The proposed rezoning is intended to allow for a long-term home for the tiny home village.
The city has not made a commitment to earmark payment in lieu of dollars for the 38th and Walnut site yet.
The payment in lieu of amount for the 335 unit project is in the range of $1.7 to $1.9 million.
The city has used the TOD Fund to assist in the purchase of the 38th and Blake site.
The TOD loan for the 38th and Blake site was paid off in 2015 or early 2016.
The proposed development includes 65 units of affordable housing on the 38th and Walnut site and 325 market rate apartments on the Blake Street side.
The affordable housing units are intended to be at 30 to 40% of the area median income.
The city has not yet finalized the process for the overlay and approval of the payment in lieu of arrangement.
The city has not yet established a formal process for the renewability of temporary use permits for tiny home villages.
The city has not yet determined the exact number of units that would satisfy the affordability requirements for the 38th and Walnut site.
The city has not yet identified a permanent home for the tiny home village.
